Born: August 29, 1958, 7:33 PM local time, Gary, Indiana, USA. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating A.

The A rating means the time comes from the person himself or a source close to him, one step below a birth certificate but still treated as reliable, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be read normally. Open Michael Jackson's chart on Astrolas to follow along.

One feature outweighs everything else in this chart. Five of his ten planets, the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Uranus and Pluto, sit in the 6th house, the part of the chart the Astrolas library ties to daily work, craft and habit. Half the chart is parked in the house of practice and repetition.

He was the youngest of the singing Jackson brothers, performing with them as a child in the late 1960s before going solo. His albums through the late 1970s, 1980s and early 1990s, including Thriller, Bad and Dangerous, made him one of the defining performers in popular music, known worldwide as the King of Pop for his singing, dancing and elaborate music videos.

doan: The Sun sits at 6°09' Virgo, Mercury, retrograde, at 25°25' Leo, Venus at 17°04' Leo, Uranus at 13°30' Leo and Pluto at 2°10' Virgo. All five land in the 6th house.

Uranus in Leo and Pluto in Virgo are generational, shared by his whole cohort of musicians born in the late 1950s, so the personal reading here comes from the house they share with the three faster-moving planets, not from those two signs alone.

The library's Virgo Sun is a sharp, detail-driven perfectionist, always working to refine itself, happiest serving others through disciplined, careful effort. In the 6th house, that same drive becomes identity: the library reads a 6th-house Sun as someone who defines themselves through their work, expects recognition for the effort it takes, and tends to keep working past the point where most people would rest.

Mercury in Leo, retrograde, brings a confident, expressive mind drawn to performance and leadership, usually in the company of others, though it can slide into stubbornness. The 6th-house Mercury wants steady, hands-on work and precision, and the library notes it usually runs at its own internal rhythm rather than on display.

Venus in Leo loves warmly and dramatically, wanting to be the center of a partner's attention, generous but craving admiration in return. In the 6th house, the library ties it to a pleasant working environment and good relationships with colleagues, important enough that this Venus struggles in a rigid or unpleasant workplace.

Taken together, five planets built for repetition, precision and performance, all stacked in the house of daily craft, line up closely with a reputation built on relentless rehearsal and total control over every detail of a show.

The Sun and Pluto are in conjunction, about four degrees apart (orb 3°59'), both in Virgo and the 6th house.

The library reads this pairing as extreme energy and an iron will, the capacity to transform yourself and to attain almost anything you set out to do, radiating an intensity that others pick up on and sometimes turn to for direction. It also reads strong intuition and a born analyst's feel for other people's psychology. The caution it names is a pull toward control, a risk of letting the drive to manage every outcome tip into something harsher.

Applied to the 6th house of craft, that reads less like personal ambition and more like control over the work itself: producing, arranging and directing his own material and performances down to the smallest detail rather than leaving the decisions to someone else.
Venus and Uranus are also in conjunction, about three and a half degrees apart (orb 3°34'), both in Leo and the 6th house.

The library calls this a lightning-strike pairing: a captivating personality, a dramatic and exciting emotional register, income and spending that swing unpredictably, and real benefit from friends, fan communities and social connection. It also names a strong, independent streak that resists being tied down.

That matches a performer whose stage presence ran on exactly that kind of electricity, who built one of the largest and most devoted fan bases in music, and who moved through dramatic highs across a long career, on stage as much as off it.

muc.ten: Saturn conjunct the Midheaven, in Sagittarius
doan: Saturn sits at 19°07' Sagittarius, in the 9th house, and the Midheaven falls at 19°31' Sagittarius. The two are in a close conjunction, about a quarter of a degree apart (orb 0°24'), the tightest contact anywhere in the chart.

The library reads this as one of the most ambitious placements there is: a relentless pursuit of status, recognition and achievement in a career, strong enough to become the organizing force of a life. It's also a test of integrity, since anything done dishonestly tends to backfire quickly, and it warns that family life can suffer when career takes up too much room.

Saturn in Sagittarius itself, in the library's reading, usually brings success late, after real perseverance, and points toward a role as a teacher or an authority whose knowledge and reputation took years of work to earn. Across a career that started in childhood and never really let up, that pattern fits: the climb toward being recognized as the defining pop performer of his era was long, continuous and famously exacting.

muc.ten: Jupiter conjunct Neptune, in the 8th house
doan: Jupiter sits at 28°32' Libra, and Neptune at 2°35' Scorpio, both in the 8th house and in conjunction, about four degrees apart (orb 4°02').

The library reads this pairing as a rich imagination paired with real luck in spiritual life and in finances, a strong sixth sense and even a touch of the psychic. The caution it names is letting kindness and idealism outrun reality: promising more than can be delivered, or trusting that things will work out rather than keeping expectations realistic.

In the 8th house of shared resources and transformation, that idealism shows up as generosity turned outward. He co-wrote and performed on "We Are the World" in 1985 and later built a foundation and a song, "Heal the World," around the same kind of oversized, hopeful ambition the library describes.

muc.ten: Moon in Pisces, rising in the 1st house
doan: The Moon sits at 14°54' Pisces, in the 1st house, the same sign as the Ascendant itself at 10°07' Pisces.

The library's Pisces Moon is sensitive, dreaming and intuitive, with real artistic gifts in music and a strong pull toward romance and compassion, though it can tip into escapism or being easily swayed by others. In the 1st house, the library reads feelings expressed outward rather than held in check, a sharp sixth sense for who is sincere, and a real need for acceptance and recognition from an audience.

The Astrolas library doesn't yet have an entry for Pisces rising itself, so this piece doesn't build a reading on the Ascendant alone, only on the Moon that shares its sign and house. Even so, an artist whose public identity ran so visibly on emotion, and who spent a career chasing the audience's embrace, lines up with what the library says a 1st-house Pisces Moon needs.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: The chart doesn't explain the talent. What it shows is where the energy went: five planets stacked in the 6th house of daily work and precision, a Sun conjunct Pluto turning that work into total control over his own material, and a Moon in Pisces that needed the audience's embrace as much as it gave something back. He died in 2009.
